parity.summary: Parity: 19991/19991 lines pass  (25786 ms, lexicon-browser-1, Node 22.23.4)
chain_sections: ok    chain: controls of the trace check: 1/1

L8.rule: all-or-nothing, separately for the JS grower (growSync) and the Python port: (a) the record equal to Owl's growBiochain field for field (and BioChain-AI's equal to Owl's), (b) Owl's and BioChain-AI's verifyIntegrity accept every record, (c) EngramCore.importBiochain accepts every record and recreates the text byte for byte, (d) the V0 id stream (SHA-256 and count), LVOCAB/1, LADDR/1 with addrTableRoot and every LPREP/1 string equal in Python and JS (the reference decides (d)); void if a control fails to show its weakness

1.what: the Python grower with BioChain-AI's shdccp_kernel.pack normalisation (0x80 written as 0x81), engrams off, against Owl's engrams-off record; must differ on at least one synthetic shard

2.what: a grower that hashes leaves over binary bytes (engrams off); must differ from Owl's record on every shard and be rejected by Owl's verifyIntegrity

3.what: one byte of every shard altered (bit 0 of its first ASCII byte), regrown: its leaf and its root must change

ms_median.note: Owl's and BioChain-AI's growers ran in 4 worker threads beside the Python half (contended); growSync and Python alone

L9.rule: exact and all-or-nothing: supported with 0 failures (undetected alterations, inclusion proofs accepted for a wrong leaf or position or rejected for the right one, failed consistency proofs, JS/Python mismatches of roots, proofs, draws or verdicts, weave failures and JS/Python weave mismatches), refuted by 1, void if a control fails to show its weakness

1.what: the shdccp/2 Merkle rule (pairwise SHA-256 over hex, odd node duplicated) gives equal roots for L and L with its last element duplicated, at every odd K >= 3 among the synthetic K (CVE-2012-2459)

2.what: an XOR summary of the leaf prefixes misses at least one adjacent swap that the exact weave detects

L10.rule: supported if there are 0 false accepts and 0 false rejects in both languages and the verdicts (selfConsistent, authentic and the failing check) are identical; refuted by any one; void when control 2 fails; a class whose control 1 fails (Owl accepts none of its records) is void and left out

1.what: Owl's verifyIntegrity, run from the Owl checkout, must accept at least one T1, one T2, one T8 and one T9 record (else that class's gap claim is withdrawn and the class is void)

2.what: Python verification without the P1363-to-DER conversion (the raw 64 bytes handed to cryptography as DER) must reject every valid signature made in this run

L11.rule: supported if the upper end of the 95% bootstrap interval of the median per-shard time is <= 250 ms; refuted if its lower end exceeds 500 ms; inconclusive otherwise; void if a timed verification's own record does not show the attestation step run inside the timed window (full) or skipped (control) — Amendment 8 item 2; the comparison of the medians with the step skipped is reported

bootstrap.by: numpy default_rng(7) in run_claims_phase3.py (rank.ci_mean's procedure, the median)

control.what: Amendment 8 item 2: the control is decided by each timed verification's own record of its checks (step_check below); the registered comparison of the medians with the attestation step skipped is reported (median_comparison_faster) and decides nothing, since a ~1 ms step cannot be resolved against the run-to-run noise

paired.what: reported, decides nothing: per shard, full minus skipped (means of repetitions 2 and 3); the interval is the 95% bootstrap interval of their median (numpy default_rng(7))

step_check.what: every timed full verification ran every check, each passed, the attestation check inside the timed window with a time > 0; every timed attestation-skipped verification recorded the attestation check as skipped (0 ms) and passed every other check (READING runner-13)

literal_laddr_per_shard.what: LADDR/1 recomputed inside each verification (Amendment 7 item 7's literal alternative; decides nothing)

other_mode_packages.what: the same shards' engrams-on records, packaged and attested the same way (Amendment 8 item 1; decides nothing)

readings.text: Amendment 8 item 1: the packages of L10 and L11 and the corpus manifest of L9(a) use the records grown with engrams off, the Lexicon's default for corpora (D4; Explainer 3: off by default for corpora and never an input). L11 on the same shards' engrams-on packages is reported and decides nothing.

Dry-run corpora: the verb shards are corpus "wordnet30-verb" and the adjective shards "wordnet30-adj" (spdx LicenseRef-WordNet-3.0 and sourceUrlSha of the archive URL, as C0); the Rng(4000 + i) synthetic shards keep "lexicon-synth-v1" with sourceUrlSha of "rng:4000+i". The verb shards stand in for C0 in L9(a), L9(b), L10 and L11.

L8 control 3: in every shard, bit 0 of the first ASCII byte is flipped (it stays ASCII, so the text stays valid UTF-8) and the text regrown with engrams off; the leaf of the chunk holding that byte and merkleRoot must both change.

L8 control 2: the grower with leaves over binary bytes (lexicon_core.js leaves: "binary", the reference's READING 10) runs with engrams off on every shard; its record is compared with Owl's engrams-off record and given to Owl's verifyIntegrity; the Python port's binary record must equal it (reported). Control 1 is the Python grower with BioChain-AI's normalisation (packets "kernel"), engrams off, against Owl's engrams-off record on the synthetic shards; the JS twin is reported.

L9(a) draws for K > 200 (the Python half's l9_draws): with replacement from Rng(2000 + j), first the 2,000 alterations, each uniform over the alterations the K <= 200 rule enumerates (the trace's order: for each i replace, delete, insert before i, swap i and i + 1, truncate to i entries; then duplicate-last), then the 2,000 consistency sizes m = 1 + below(K - 1) (K = 1000 has only 999 sizes m < N). A replacement entry is entry i with its first byte XOR 1, an insertion 32 zero bytes (the trace's). For K <= 200 every m in 1..N - 1 (RFC 9162 has no proof from m = 0).

L9 control 2 checks every adjacent swap of the synthetic lists for K <= 200 and the first and last (i = 0 and K - 2) for K = 1000 and 1001 (a weave of 1,001 prefixes takes 0.15 s in JS and 0.3 s in Python; the control needs one swap that the XOR misses and the weave detects).

L8(b) and (c) "every record": per shard and mode, the distinct records among growSync's, the Python port's, Owl's and BioChain-AI's (equal records are verified once). A rejection of growSync's, Owl's or BioChain-AI's record counts against the JS grower, of the Python port's, Owl's or BioChain-AI's against the Python port. BioChain-AI's record differing from Owl's counts against both (claim (a): "BioChain-AI's gives the same"). (d) is decided by the reference, so a (d) mismatch counts against the JS grower.
Dry-run L10 clean set: 22 verb shards cannot give 50 distinct indices, so Rng(4000 + i).below(22) is drawn until all 22 are; each tamper record draws its clean package with below(22).

L10 tamper places, record j of class k from Rng(base + 50(k - 1) + j) after its clean package below(n): T2 frame below(K), then bit below(32) of its crystal32 (word bit 24 + bit), parity re-fixed; T7 frames below(K - 1) and the next; T9 frame below(K), drawn again from the same Rng until the frame has a single-bit residual flip that decodes the same (spike S4's search, in its order), then that flip below(count). T3 (lvocabHash) and T8 (chainId) change the last hex digit, S4's rule as in the trace. T4 is attested by the key the registry marks revoked. T5 takes the attestation of the next clean package in draw order ((c + 1) mod n). T6 is the Tier-P package of the same shard (a Tier-P twin of the corpus, each shard j salted with the test salt of j, its own LCORPUS/1 and LGROW/1, attested by the active key) checked with the salt of shard index + 1, the next shard's, as the trace reads "the salt of shard j + 1".

L11 protocol: repetition-major passes over the shards; in each pass a shard's full verification and its attestation-skipped verification run back to back, the order alternating, so drift affects both alike; a shard's time is the mean of its repetitions 2 and 3, the median is over shards, and the control compares the two medians. The package is passed as the parsed object (JSON parsing is not one of the hardened checks). The session (LVOCAB/1, LADDR/1 recomputed from WordNet, the registry snapshot loaded) is timed once and counted once in the 1,000-shard estimate.

L11's control, "otherwise the step is not being timed and the test is void", is also read from each timed verification's own record of its checks: every full verification must hold every check passed with the attestation check's time > 0 inside the timed window, and every attestation-skipped one the attestation check recorded as skipped (0 ms) with every other check passed; otherwise L11 is void (not registered: it can only void, never support). The registered comparison of the two medians still decides the control. In this run the attestation step measures 2.995 ms against a single verification's spread of about 20.95 ms, and the paired interval (full minus skipped) is [-4.583, 2.124] ms, which includes 0: the comparison of the medians is within the noise, so it can fail by chance with the step timed (L11 void) and pass by chance with the step not run (which the step check catches). The registration fixes no power for the comparison; a comparison powered against the noise needs an amendment.
